title: Short-window overflow-lane gateway and billing attenuation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a short-window overflow-lane gateway (aka 'overflow gateway') that temporarily accepts requests routed off primary dedicated fleets when SLOs or capacity headroom are breached. The gateway provides configurable tenant-level controls, operator overrides, and a billing attenuation mechanism that issues provisional credits or prorated charges for burst usage.

Goals: 1) Keep latency-sensitive customer traffic online during short spikes without forcing immediate vertical scaling or long-term capacity commitments. 2) Make billing for temporary boosts transparent, auditable, and predictable for customers and finance. 3) Provide operators with safe knobs (quarantine, drain, emergency cutover) and visibility for post-mortems.

Scope: - Overflow gateway service (stateless front layer) that routes to surge pool instances or preemptible cloud lanes. - Per-tenant config: max overflow QPS, grace-window (seconds), attenuation curve (credit percentage based on duration and volume). - Metering: fine-grained tags on each overflow request (tenant, route, model, sequence_length_bucket) persisted to the billing ledger. - Operator API & console views: active overflow sessions, estimated provisional credit, and one-click evacuation. - Billing pipeline integration: provisional credits ledger, reconciliation job, and customer-facing invoice line item.

Technical design notes: - Routing: integrate with Smart Routing so requests are routed to overflow gateway when (1) primary fleet utilization > threshold and (2) predicted tail latency risk > risk_threshold. - Autoscaling interplay: overflow gateway should be invoked before triggering expensive permanent scale-ups; update autoscaler policy to treat overflow usage as input to scale decisions with a decay window. - Surge pool composition: mixture of dedicated spare nodes, preemptible instances, and burst lanes with lower SLO. The gateway marks calls routed to lower-tier lanes with explicit metadata so Console and metrics show SLO-class for each token. - Billing attenuation: apply a tiered attenuation curve; first 30s entirely discounted, next N minutes discounted at X%, and an upper bound where full charge applies. Business logic captured in attenuation functions. - Safety: default tenant limits to avoid noisy-neighbor exhaustion; global circuit-breaker to stop overflow routing if surge pool health degrades. - Auditability: every overflow decision emits an event to the audit stream with reasoning (utilization snapshot, model variant, routing policy id).

Operational runbook (high-level): 1) Detection: Alert when overflow gateway utilization > 70% for 5m or when provisional credit exposure > $5k for any tenant. 2) Inspect: Use console view to identify top routes/tenants and examine sequence_length distribution. 3) Mitigate: (a) Tighten per-tenant overflow caps, (b) Evacuate specific tenants via operator API, (c) Temporarily increase dedicated pool reservation for high-value tenants. 4) Post-incident: Run reconciliation to convert provisional credits into final invoice adjustments and annotate incident in billing ledger.

Observability & metrics: - Per-tenant overflow_qps, overflow_token_rate, p50/p95 latency by lane, error-rate by lane. - Billing exposure metric: provisional_credit_estimate_usd (rolling 1h/24h). - SLO impact: fraction of requests served from >primary-lane. Dashboards: link to internal dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/overflow-gateway/overview (placeholder).

Testing plan: - Unit tests for attenuation math and routing decision logic. - Integration test harness that replays production spike traces to verify: routing correctness, autoscaler backoff signals, and ledger entries created. - Billing e2e: simulate tenant with repeated overflow events and validate provisional credits, reconciliation, and final invoice line.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary with internal tenants only for 2 weeks (small sample of low-risk tenants). 2) Opt-in beta for selected customers (with explicit consent and visibility). 3) Gradual default-on for small tenants with conservative caps. 4) Full default for all tenants after 90 days and one reconciliation audit.

Open decisions: - Exact attenuation curve parameters (product to propose recommended defaults). - Whether to expose attenuation controls in self-serve Console or limit to account managers for first 90 days. - Billing UX: single provisional invoice line vs. detailed per-session log.

Links & artifacts: - Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Overflow+Gateway+Design (draft) - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/overflow-gateway/pull/42 - Billing worker PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/198 - Spike test traces: gs://redwood-test-data/overflow-spikes/2025-10-logs.tar.gz

Next steps: 1) PM to finalize attenuation defaults and UX by 2025-12-01. 2) Core eng to land routing prototype and unit tests (ENG-188501-1) and open canary runbook (ENG-188501-2). 3) Billing to implement provisional ledger integration and reconciliation job.
